text: At its 106th plenary session, held on 11 and 12 March 2016, the Venice Commission (European Commission for Democracy through Law) adopted an Opinion on Articles 216, 299, 301 and 314 of the Penal Code of Turkey (CDL-AD(2016)002).
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that the Penal Code of Turkey does not contain a definition of an armed organisation or an armed group.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that in its judgment E. 2006/10-253 K. 2007/80 of 3 April 2007, the General Criminal Board of the Court of Cassation of Turkey listed the main criteria that a criminal organisation for the purposes of Article 220 of the Penal Code should display, including: at least three members; a tight or loose hierarchical connection between members; a common intention to commit crimes; continuity in time; and sufficient structure, number of members, tools and equipment for the commission of the envisaged crimes.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that the Court of Cassation of Turkey developed the criterion of 'membership' in an armed organisation by examining different acts of the suspect, taking account of their 'continuity, diversity and intensity' in order to see whether those acts prove an 'organic relationship' with the organisation or whether the acts may be considered as committed knowingly and wilfully within the 'hierarchical structure' of the organisation.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that if an 'organic relationship' with the organisation cannot be proven on the basis of acts attributed to the defendant which do not present any 'continuity, diversity or intensity', the paragraphs on 'aiding and abetting an armed organisation' or 'committing crime on behalf of an armed organisation' under Article 220 of the Penal Code may be applied.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that acts such as 'participating in a public demonstration following a general call from pro-PKK media outlets, making victory sign and shouting slogans to support and in favour of the leader of a terrorist organisation, clashing with the security forces and forming barricades' are considered crimes committed on behalf of an organisation and not as membership.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 recommended that the established criteria in the case law of the Court of Cassation of Turkey — that acts attributed to a defendant should show 'in their continuity, diversity and intensity' an 'organic relationship' to an organisation or prove that the defendant acted knowingly and willingly within the 'hierarchical structure' of the organisation — should be applied strictly.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that the loose application of the criteria of 'continuity, diversity and intensity' and 'organic relationship' may give rise to issues concerning in particular the principle of legality within the meaning of Article 7 of the Convention.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that the expression of an opinion in its different forms should not be the only evidence before domestic courts to decide on the membership of the defendant in an armed organisation.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that where the only evidence consists of forms of expression, a conviction for being a member of an armed organisation would constitute an interference with the right of the defendants to freedom of expression, and that the necessity of this interference should be examined in the concrete circumstances of each case on the basis of the criteria set forth in the case-law of the ECtHR, in particular the criterion of 'incitement to violence'.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that in a judgment of 4 March 2008 the General Criminal Board of the Court of Cassation of Turkey held that acts such as participating in a public demonstration following a general call from pro-PKK media outlets, making a victory sign and shouting slogans to support and in favour of the leader of a terrorist organisation, and clashing with the security forces, are considered crimes committed on behalf of the terrorist organisation.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that in the judgment of 4 March 2008, although membership in an armed organisation was not established, the defendant was convicted as a member of a criminal organisation according to Article 220 § 6 of the Penal Code applied in conjunction with Article 314.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that by the judgment of 4 March 2008, the Court of Cassation of Turkey annulled the decision of the Diyarbakır Assize Court which had considered that in order for a court to conclude that a crime was committed on behalf of an organisation, the latter must have called for action not to an undefined collective, but rather to an individual person who is capable of directly committing that act.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that a new paragraph was added to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713 by an amendment of 11 April 2013, providing that those who committed the crimes indicated in section 7(2) of Law no. 3713, section 6(2) of Law no. 3713, and section 28(1) of the Public Demonstrations Law no. 2911 shall not be sentenced separately under Article 220(6) of the Penal Code.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 welcomed the amendment introduced to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713, which excluded the above-mentioned crimes from the scope of application of Article 220(6) of the Penal Code.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 considered that the scope of the amendment to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713 is rather limited and does not provide for sufficient protection to the exercise of freedom of expression and assembly.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that some forms of expression may also fall under the scope of Article 220(7) of the Penal Code (aiding and abetting an organisation), which could lead to abusive application in practice since a form of expression considered as being in support of an organisation may be sanctioned under Article 220(7) instead of Article 220(6) in order to sentence defendants as if they were members of an armed organisation under Article 314, although their organic relationship with an armed organisation is not established.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that the new paragraph added to Article 7 of the Anti-Terror Law no. 3713 refers to section 28(1) of the Law on Public Demonstrations, which merely criminalises the organisation of or participation in unlawful public demonstrations, while the crime regulated under Article 32(1) of the Law on Public Demonstrations (refusing to obey the warnings of the security forces during a public demonstration to disperse) may still fall under the scope of Article 220(6) of the Penal Code in conjunction with Article 314.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 recommended that the sentence 'although he is not a member of that organisation, shall also be sentenced for the offence of being a member of that organisation' in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 of the Penal Code be repealed, so that those who commit the crimes indicated in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 would not be sanctioned as members of an armed organisation under Article 314, but by other, separate sanctions.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)

text: The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that should the sentence in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Article 220 be maintained, the Turkish authorities should consider limiting the application of Article 220 in conjunction with Article 314 to cases which do not involve the exercise of the rights to freedom of expression and assembly.
section_path: THE FACTS
III. RELEVANT INTERNATIONAL MATERIALS
A. European Commission for Democracy through Law (the Venice Commission)
